input.command:
cd /opt/nxeon-staging-hostnamefix && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix hostname collisions: unique constraint + randomized default + live checkout validation

Production ended up with 7 unrelated customers all named "web-01" — every
VPS checkout that left the hostname field blank got that exact same
hardcoded literal, with nothing checking a customer-typed name for
collision either. A hostname-keyed support script then grabbed the wrong
customer's server mid-incident (2026-09-24), surfacing one customer's
SSH port/status while working a different customer's ticket.

Backend (lib/hostname.ts, Server.hostname @unique in prisma/schema.prisma):
- normalizeHostname/isHostnameConflict/resolveUniqueHostname/isHostnameTaken,
  used by every Server-creating path (VPS, game, NxCloud, admin free-grant,
  e2e script) so a collision auto-suffixes at checkout instead of crashing,
  or is refused with a clear error where auto-suffixing would be confusing
  (admin grant, ops scripts).
- Every hostname-keyed lookup audited and hardened to refuse/disambiguate
  on multiple matches instead of blindly picking one
  (scripts/recover-errored-server.mjs, scripts/backfill-claude.ts), plus
  scripts/find-duplicate-hostnames.ts + dedupe-hostnames.ts to help resolve
  the existing prod duplicates before the @unique migration lands (that
  migration + timing is being handled separately by the platform owner).

Checkout UX (this pass, per explicit owner direction — supersedes the
previous silent-auto-suffix-only approach):
- lib/hostname-shared.ts splits the pure, DB-free helpers (format/reserved
  rules, normalization, random suffix, genDefaultVpsHostname) out of
  lib/hostname.ts so the client-side checkout wizard can import them
  without pulling Prisma into the browser bundle.
- VPS checkout (components/nx/order.tsx, components/nx/DeployView.tsx) now
  pre-fills a randomized "vps-xxxx" default instead of the fixed "web-01"
  literal, exactly like the field was always pre-filled before.
- lib/actions-hostname-check.ts adds a live availability check
  (checkHostnameAvailable), wired into the Hostname field with a 400ms
  debounce: an already-taken name shakes the field, shows an inline "This
  hostname is already taken" error, and BLOCKS Next / the final pay button
  until it's fixed — mirrors the existing gameSubCheck/hostSubCheck idiom,
  but deliberately stricter (those are advisory-only). The "Server
  settings" fold auto-reopens if it was collapsed so a live collision is
  never hidden from the customer it's blocking.
- Backend resolveUniqueHostname stays as defense-in-depth (residual-race
  P2002 catch is unchanged) for any path that doesn't go through the live
  check.
- Game-server checkout confirmed NOT to have the same bug: it already
  leaves the field blank/optional and generates "<family>-<rand>"
  server-side (lib/game-order.ts's randSuffix) rather than a fixed literal
  — no change needed there.

Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, existing test suite unchanged (1382 pass /
40 pre-existing unrelated failures, identical before and after — confirmed
via git stash diff). Manually drove the real checkout wizard end-to-end
against an isolated throwaway local DB (Playwright): confirmed the
pre-filled "vps-xxxx" default, the shake/red-border/inline-error on a
known-taken name, Next being blocked, and the field clearing/unblocking
once fixed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

content.text: Chapter marked: "Verification and commit". Continue your current work.

## Summary

Built on top of the earlier pass in `/opt/nxeon-staging-hostnamefix` (branch `fix/hostname-uniqueness`) rather than redoing it — kept all of its backend work (`Server.hostname @unique`, `lib/hostname.ts`'s `resolveUniqueHostname`/`isHostnameTaken`/`isHostnameConflict`, and the hardened `scripts/recover-errored-server.mjs`/`scripts/backfill-claude.ts` lookups) and layered the new owner-directed checkout UX on top. Committed as `9e9a4f7b0f` on `fix/hostname-uniqueness` — **not pushed**. I double-checked: this repo has an active `post-commit` hook that auto-pushes `main` to GitHub, but it only ever pushes `main` (unchanged, since I committed to the feature branch), confirmed via `origin/main == main` and no new entry in `/var/log/nxeon-git-push.log`.

**What changed, by file:**
- `/opt/nxeon-staging-hostnamefix/lib/hostname-shared.ts` (new) — pure, DB-free helpers split out of `lib/hostname.ts` (format rules, `normalizeHostname`, `randHostnameSuffix`, `isHostnameConflict`, and the new `genDefaultVpsHostname`), so the client-side checkout wizard can import a default-generator without pulling Prisma into the browser bundle. `lib/hostname.ts` re-exports everything, so no existing server-side import broke.
- `/opt/nxeon-staging-hostnamefix/lib/actions-hostname-check.ts` (new) — `checkHostnameAvailable`, a `"use server"` live-check action mirroring the existing `checkGameSubdomain`/`checkHostingSubdomain` idiom.
- `/opt/nxeon-staging-hostnamefix/components/nx/order.tsx` — `seedOrder` now pre-fills `vps-xxxx` (via `genDefaultVpsHostname`) instead of the literal `"web-01"`; added a `hostCheck` state + 400ms-debounced availability effect inside `OrderProvider` (shared via context so both the wizard's Next button and the payment button see it); the VPS "configure" step's `done` flag now requires `hostCheck.status !== "bad"`.
- `/opt/nxeon-staging-hostnamefix/components/nx/DeployView.tsx` — Hostname field wired to `hostCheck`: taken name → `field-bad` (shake + red border, existing CSS) + inline "This hostname is already taken — try another."; checking/ok status icons match the existing subdomain-check pattern; `PaymentSlide`'s `ready` also gated on the check so the final pay button can't be clicked with a stale bad value; added an effect to auto-reopen the collapsed "Server settings" fold when a collision is detected (a gap I found during manual testing — otherwise the blocking error could be hidden off-screen).
- `/opt/nxeon-staging-hostnamefix/lib/order.ts` — backend blank-field fallback prefix changed from `"web"` to `"vps"` for consistency; kept as defense-in-depth, the live check is not the only guard.
- Game-server checkout (`lib/game-order.ts`, `components/customer/GameDeployWizard.tsx`) — confirmed it does **not** have the fixed-literal bug: it already leaves the field blank/optional and generates `<family>-<rand>` server-side. No change made there; I deliberately did not extend the shake/live-check UX to it since it uses a different (non-`field-bad`) validation convention and wasn't explicitly in scope for that part — flagging as a possible follow-up if wanted.

**Verification performed:**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- `npm test`: 1382 pass / 40 fail, and via a `git stash` A/B diff I confirmed the exact same 40 failing test names exist with and without my changes (pre-existing, environment-dependent, unrelated to hostnames) — zero regressions.
- Real UI check, not just compile-trust: spun up an isolated throwaway Postgres DB (`nxeon_hfverify`, dropped afterward) and a local `next dev` instance on `127.0.0.1:3099` (no shared secrets, no staging/prod DB touched), seeded a colliding `Server` row, and drove the actual checkout wizard with Playwright. Confirmed: the hostname field loads pre-filled with a random `vps-xxxx` value; typing the taken name shakes the field red and shows the inline error; Next is blocked with a "Fill in the highlighted fields to continue" hint; fixing the name shows a green check and un-blocks Next through to the Region step; collapsing the fold and reintroducing a collision auto-reopens it. All temp files (`.env`, fixture/verify scripts) and the temp DB/role were removed afterward — worktree is clean.

**Still needs a human decision (unchanged from the original task framing):** resolving the 7 existing "web-01" prod duplicates and the timing of actually applying the `@unique` migration — the owner is handling that separately, and I didn't touch prod data or that migration's timing.
